national_headline: 15 of 23 areas have an actionable cancer-pathway gap, while 4,049 of 14,774 lung cancer patients (27.4%, 16.4% to 43.1% by county, 2019–2023) lack a 12-month treatment record — separating where to change care now from where to audit records first.

indicators.label: Breast screening attendance
indicators.desc: Attended mammography screening, % of invited women (age-group programme).
indicators.caveat: Invitation coverage and cohort composition differ between counties; private mammography is not counted.

indicators.label: Cervical screening attendance
indicators.desc: Attended cervical screening, % of invited (age-group programme).
indicators.caveat: Opportunistic tests outside the programme are not counted as attendance.

indicators.label: Colorectal screening attendance
indicators.desc: Returned a FIT kit, % of persons picked for the programme (programme launched 2022).
indicators.caveat: Programme is being rolled out by birth cohort; early years cover the youngest cohorts only.

indicators.label: Missing outcome after breast referral
indicators.desc: Referred to specialist care after screening, but final diagnosis missing in the screening register (%).
indicators.caveat: Measures register completeness, not clinical care.

indicators.label: Colonoscopy after positive FIT (referral proxy)
indicators.desc: Attended colonoscopy, % of screening test positives. Proxy for completed referral to specialist diagnostics; it does not measure referral delay.
indicators.caveat: Clinical exclusions, colonoscopies outside the programme and late registrations count as non-attendance.

indicators.label: Colposcopy after referral (referral proxy)
indicators.desc: Attended colposcopy, % of those referred from age-group cervical screening. Proxy for completed referral to specialist diagnostics.
indicators.caveat: Small denominators in some counties; colposcopies done outside the programme may be missing.

indicators.label: Lung: curative treatment
indicators.desc: Patients with recorded curative treatment (surgery, chemoradiation or stereotactic RT) within 12 months, %.
indicators.caveat: Not adjusted for stage, age or comorbidity; 47.7% of lung cancers nationally lack stage information.

indicators.label: Lung: life-prolonging treatment
indicators.desc: Patients with recorded life-prolonging (non-curative) drug or radiotherapy within 12 months, %.
indicators.caveat: Higher or lower is not inherently better without stage information.

indicators.label: Lung: symptomatic care
indicators.desc: Patients with recorded symptomatic care, %. Categories overlap.
indicators.caveat: Interpretation depends on stage and frailty, which are not adjusted for.

indicators.label: Lung: no treatment record
indicators.desc: Patients with no recorded treatment of any kind within 12 months of diagnosis, %.
indicators.caveat: Missing records do not prove absence of treatment; mixes untreated patients and recording gaps.

indicators.label: Lung: MDT discussion recorded
indicators.desc: Patients with a recorded multidisciplinary team (MDT) meeting code (WZC15/WZC20), %.
indicators.caveat: Near-zero values cannot distinguish low recording from actual MDT practice. Not published for 4 counties; the comparator covers reporting counties only.

indicators.label: Lung: curative vs symptomatic-care ratio (referral proxy)
indicators.desc: Patients with recorded curative treatment per patient with recorded symptomatic care, lung cancer 2019–2023. A low ratio suggests patients reach specialist care late (late detection or referral) or lack treatment access.
indicators.caveat: Categories overlap (a patient can have both); not stage-adjusted; approximate CI ignores the overlap.
indicators.proxy_for: Timeliness of referral (patients reaching specialist care while still curable)

indicators.label: 5-yr relative survival: Lung (men)
indicators.desc: Age-standardised 5-year relative survival, lung (men) cancer, diagnosed 2020–2024 (period method).
indicators.caveat: Wide intervals in small counties; reflects stage at diagnosis as well as treatment. Compared with the national value (counts needed for a leave-one-out comparator are not published).

indicators.label: Mortality: Lung (men)
indicators.desc: Age-standardised cancer mortality per 100 000, lung (men), 2020–2024.
indicators.caveat: Driven by incidence (e.g. smoking history) as well as care quality. Compared with the national value.

national_actions.title: National EHR-to-Registry Automation & HILMO WZC15/WZC20 Coding Fix
national_actions.owner: THL, Finnish Cancer Registry (FCR), Regional Cancer Centres (FICAN) & 21 HVA CIOs
national_actions.annual_volume: ≈1,297 patient charts to audit across 16 areas
national_actions.target: Eliminate the 27.4% missing lung treatment-record blind spot and cut missing TNM stage from 47.7% toward ≤10% (≥90% automated clinical notifications by 2030, Roadmap 3.2.1).
national_actions.timeline: Chart audit of the latest diagnosis year within 3 months; coding fixes within 6 months; notification automation by 2030

citations.label: Finnish Cancer Registry, lung cancer quality report 2019–2023 (MDT recording and missing stage)
National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 3.2.1 (90% coverage incl. stage; automated clinical notifications)
Finnish Cancer Registry, clinical notification statistics by wellbeing services county

national_actions.title: National Fast-Track Lung Pathway & 4-Timestamp Referral Pilot
national_actions.owner: Ministry of Social Affairs and Health (STM), FICAN Thoracic Oncology Groups & County Pathway Leads
national_actions.annual_volume: ≈30 patients a year short of the rest-of-Finland curative rate across 5 areas
national_actions.target: Standardise direct GP-to-chest-CT routes (Roadmap 2.5.2) and establish the missing national primary-to-specialist referral-to-treatment timestamp series (Roadmap 3.1.2).
national_actions.timeline: Coordinator and referral criteria within 6 months; timestamps from month 3; curative share re-measured on the next registry quality report
national_actions.goal: Goal 3.1.2; Swedish guidance is an external model, not a Finnish target

citations.label: National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 2.5.2 (standardised referral criteria, direct investigation routes)
National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 3.1.2 (cancer-specific pathways and target times)

Regional cancer centres in Sweden, standardised care pathway (SVF) example

national_actions.title: Mandatory FICAN Quality-Manual Reminders & Multilingual Outreach in Procurement
national_actions.owner: National Cancer Screening Steering Group, FCR Mass Screening Registry & County Procurement Leads
national_actions.annual_volume: ≈52,527 invited people who did not attend across 12 areas
national_actions.target: Enforce 6-week automated reminders, Suomi.fi multilingual invitations and HPV self-sampling in every county contract (Roadmap 2.4.1 & 2.4.5), targeting the 20–22 pp non-domestic language gap.
national_actions.timeline: Reminder workflow live within 3 months; effect read from the next annual screening statistics (12–18 months)
national_actions.goal: Goal 2; supporting detection pathway, not sufficient as the only Goal 3 measure

national_actions.title: Closed-Loop Positive-Screen Follow-Up & Monthly Endoscopy/Colposcopy Reporting
national_actions.owner: FCR Screening Register, YTA Endoscopy & Gynaecology Leads
national_actions.annual_volume: ≈1,615 FIT positives without a recorded colonoscopy across 9 areas
national_actions.target: Mandate 2-week screening-nurse callbacks (§11.2.1) and monthly colonoscopy/colposcopy outcome feeds (§12.5, Roadmap 2.4.5) so screen-positive patients never drop out across municipal/HVA moves.

national_actions.goal: Detection-to-diagnosis; prospective times can support Goal 3 pathway monitoring

actions.title: Peer review of a survival or mortality gap
actions.owner: County cancer centre lead with the collaboration-area (YTA) quality group
actions.target: Lung (women) mortality moving toward the national value (24.7 /100k; now 34.6 /100k) in the next annual Cancer in Finland release; one agreed pathway change implemented within 12 months
actions.annual_volume: ≈22 cancer deaths a year in scope (109 over 5 years, 2020–2024)
actions.timeline: Peer review within 6 months; annual re-measurement
first_90_days: Choose the peer county and agree a data-exchange template
Pull stage, diagnostic route and treatment mix for the cancer with the gap
Schedule the joint review with both counties' clinical leads
concrete_steps: Pick a peer county with a similar population profile and a better outcome for the same cancer (the snapshot lists demographic peers) and exchange aggregate pathway data. Suggested peer: Ostrobothnia (Lung (women) mortality 20.4 /100k).
Compare stage at diagnosis, the share with histological confirmation, the diagnostic route and the treatment mix for the cancer with the gap.
Check whether the gap is explained by incidence or risk factors (mortality reflects incidence as well as care) before attributing it to the pathway.
Agree one concrete pathway change with a named owner and record it with the YTA quality group.
Re-measure every year; national peer reviews are held once a year (roadmap 3.2.2), and persistent gaps go to the response mechanism in roadmap 3.2.3.
actions.escalation: If the gap persists for two consecutive annual releases, report it to the regional cancer centre under roadmap action 3.2.3 (response to peer-review findings).

actions.title: Close the loop after a positive FIT
actions.owner: County screening and endoscopy leads
actions.baseline: Colonoscopy after positive FIT (referral proxy): 65.5% (171 of 261), 2024; rest of Finland 72.9%
actions.target: Colonoscopy recorded for at least 72.9% of FIT positives (rest of Finland rate; now 65.5%); a documented reason for every remaining case
actions.annual_volume: ≈90 FIT positives without a recorded colonoscopy in 2024 (261 − 171)
actions.timeline: Reconciliation within 3 months; nurse call-back permanent; re-measure on the next annual statistics
first_90_days: Pull the list of FIT positives without a recorded colonoscopy
Reconcile against endoscopy and HILMO records and code a reason for each case
Start the two-week screening-nurse call-back
Agree monthly reporting of colonoscopy results to the screening register
concrete_steps: List every FIT-positive person in the latest programme year without a recorded colonoscopy and reconcile each against endoscopy-unit and HILMO records (colonoscopies outside the programme count as completed follow-up).

Record a reason for every unresolved case: declined, clinically excluded, examined elsewhere, moved county after the positive test (the screening chain breaks on a move, colorectal manual §11.3), or lost to follow-up.
Make the screening nurse phone every positive person who has not made contact within about two weeks, as colorectal manual §11.2.1 requires.
Send completed colonoscopies to the screening register monthly (roadmap 2.4.5) so the loop closes visibly.
Record the date of the positive result and of the colonoscopy for every case and report the median and 90th-percentile interval quarterly.
actions.escalation: If verified non-attendance persists after the call-back, review endoscopy capacity and travel distance with the collaboration-area endoscopy units and report to the YTA screening steering group.

concrete_steps: Stratify the county's latest breast, cervical and colorectal screening attendance by native language (Finnish, Swedish, other) and municipality so strong county averages do not mask pockets with 20+ pp lower uptake.

Verify that screening data are reported monthly to the Finnish Cancer Registry (roadmap 2.4.5) and that automated clinical notifications incl. TNM stage progress toward the 90% 2030 target (roadmap 3.2.1).

Start prospective recording of the four cancer-pathway timestamps (referral received, first specialist contact, diagnosis, treatment start) to close the national referral-delay data gap (roadmap 3.1.2).
Participate as a benchmark peer in the collaboration-area (YTA) annual quality review (roadmap 3.2.2) and watch any monitor-level indicators on the next registry release.
actions.escalation: If sub-county language or municipal screening gaps exceed 10 percentage points or any monitor indicator crosses outside the 95% CI, activate the stage-specific action playbook immediately.

actions.title: Raise screening participation with reminders and accessible invitations
actions.owner: County screening programme lead
actions.baseline: Breast screening attendance: 76.1% (22,860 of 30,039), 2024; rest of Finland 82.1%; also Bowel screening 71.5% vs 73.7%
actions.target: Breast screening at or above the rest of Finland rate (82.1%; now 76.1%) in the next programme round; a reminder sent to 100% of eligible non-attenders
actions.annual_volume: ≈7,179 invited people who did not attend in 2024 (30,039 − 22,860)
actions.timeline: Reminder workflow live within 3 months; effect read from the next annual screening statistics (12–18 months)
first_90_days: Name the programme owner and pull the latest non-attender list
Audit undeliverable invitations and the invitation language
Switch on the automated reminder (6 weeks breast and colorectal, 4–8 weeks cervical)
Agree monthly participation reporting with the Finnish Cancer Registry (roadmap 2.4.5)
concrete_steps: Pull the non-attender list for the latest programme round from the screening register and break it down by language (Finnish, Swedish, other), age group and postcode area.
Audit invitation delivery (undeliverable letters, outdated addresses) so delivery failures are not counted as refusals.

Automate the reminder in the invitation system: breast, a reminder invitation 6 weeks after the first (breast manual §6.4); colorectal, a reminder letter with a free replacement kit if no sample arrives within 6 weeks (colorectal manual §10.5); cervical, a reminder 4–8 weeks after the first invitation (cervical manual §8.3).
Send invitations and reminders in the person's registered language using the Finnish Cancer Registry templates (Finnish, Swedish, English), and through suomi.fi where the person has enabled it.
For cervical screening, offer a pre-booked time and place and an HPV self-sampling kit to non-attenders after the reminder (cervical manual §8.4).
Write the reminder requirements into the screening service procurement contract (roadmap action 2.4.1).
actions.escalation: If participation stays below the rest-of-Finland rate after one round with reminders, commission an equity analysis by language and area and take it to the collaboration-area (YTA) screening steering group.

citations.label: FICAN colorectal screening quality manual 2026, §10.5 reminder letter
FICAN breast screening quality manual 2026, §6.4 reminder invitation
FICAN cervical screening quality manual 2026, §8.3–8.4 reminder and self-sampling
National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 2.4.1 (quality manuals in procurement)

actions.title: Verify lung treatment, stage and MDT records
actions.owner: County oncology lead and registry/data team
actions.baseline: Lung: no treatment record: 28.5% (302 of 1,058), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 27.3%; also MDT recorded 0.2% vs 7.4%
actions.target: No lung treatment record back in line with the rest of Finland rate (27.3%; now 28.5%) after record reconciliation; stage recorded for at least 90% of new cases (roadmap 3.2.1)
actions.annual_volume: ≈60 patient charts to audit a year (302 patients without a treatment record over 5 years, 2019–2023)
actions.timeline: Chart audit of the latest diagnosis year within 3 months; coding fixes within 6 months; notification automation by 2030
first_90_days: Pull the list of lung cancer patients without a treatment record for the latest diagnosis year
Reconcile against oncology, surgery, radiotherapy and palliative care records
Check WZC15/WZC20 coding of MDT meetings
Report corrected records to the Finnish Cancer Registry
concrete_steps: Pull the county's lung cancer patients without any HILMO treatment record within 12 months of diagnosis and review each chart: treated in another county, treated but not coded, best supportive care decision, or died before treatment.
Check that MDT meetings are coded in HILMO with WZC15/WZC20 even when the patient is not present; the lung quality report notes that only direct patient contacts reach HILMO.

Audit the clinical cancer notification (kliininen syöpäilmoitus) to the Finnish Cancer Registry for the stage (TNM) field; nationally stage is missing for 47.7% (7,097 of 14,873, 2019–2023) of lung cancers.
Automate the clinical notification from the oncology record (roadmap 3.2.1 targets 90% automated notifications by 2030 and 90% data coverage including stage).
For breast screening referrals with a missing outcome, send the final diagnosis back to the screening register.
Send corrected records to the registry and re-run this snapshot before judging treatment rates.
actions.escalation: If the share without a record stays above the rest-of-Finland rate after reconciliation, treat it as a care gap: start a clinical review of untreated patients (pathway_coordination playbook).

National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 3.2.1 (90% coverage incl. stage; automated clinical notifications)
Finnish Cancer Registry, clinical notification statistics by wellbeing services county

actions.title: Raise screening participation with reminders and accessible invitations
actions.owner: County screening programme lead
actions.baseline: Breast screening attendance: 76.8% (12,323 of 16,057), 2024; rest of Finland 81.8%; also Bowel screening 71.3% vs 73.6%
actions.target: Breast screening at or above the rest of Finland rate (81.8%; now 76.8%) in the next programme round; a reminder sent to 100% of eligible non-attenders
actions.annual_volume: ≈3,734 invited people who did not attend in 2024 (16,057 − 12,323)
actions.timeline: Reminder workflow live within 3 months; effect read from the next annual screening statistics (12–18 months)
first_90_days: Name the programme owner and pull the latest non-attender list
Audit undeliverable invitations and the invitation language
Switch on the automated reminder (6 weeks breast and colorectal, 4–8 weeks cervical)
Agree monthly participation reporting with the Finnish Cancer Registry (roadmap 2.4.5)
concrete_steps: Pull the non-attender list for the latest programme round from the screening register and break it down by language (Finnish, Swedish, other), age group and postcode area.
Audit invitation delivery (undeliverable letters, outdated addresses) so delivery failures are not counted as refusals.

Automate the reminder in the invitation system: breast, a reminder invitation 6 weeks after the first (breast manual §6.4); colorectal, a reminder letter with a free replacement kit if no sample arrives within 6 weeks (colorectal manual §10.5); cervical, a reminder 4–8 weeks after the first invitation (cervical manual §8.3).
Send invitations and reminders in the person's registered language using the Finnish Cancer Registry templates (Finnish, Swedish, English), and through suomi.fi where the person has enabled it.
For cervical screening, offer a pre-booked time and place and an HPV self-sampling kit to non-attenders after the reminder (cervical manual §8.4).
Write the reminder requirements into the screening service procurement contract (roadmap action 2.4.1).
actions.escalation: If participation stays below the rest-of-Finland rate after one round with reminders, commission an equity analysis by language and area and take it to the collaboration-area (YTA) screening steering group.

actions.title: Peer review of a survival or mortality gap
actions.owner: County cancer centre lead with the collaboration-area (YTA) quality group
actions.target: Lung (women) mortality moving toward the national value (24.7 /100k; now 30.3 /100k) in the next annual Cancer in Finland release; one agreed pathway change implemented within 12 months
actions.annual_volume: ≈40 cancer deaths a year in scope (202 over 5 years, 2020–2024)
actions.timeline: Peer review within 6 months; annual re-measurement
first_90_days: Choose the peer county and agree a data-exchange template
Pull stage, diagnostic route and treatment mix for the cancer with the gap
Schedule the joint review with both counties' clinical leads
concrete_steps: Pick a peer county with a similar population profile and a better outcome for the same cancer (the snapshot lists demographic peers) and exchange aggregate pathway data. Suggested peer: Southwest Finland (Lung (women) mortality 24.3 /100k).
Compare stage at diagnosis, the share with histological confirmation, the diagnostic route and the treatment mix for the cancer with the gap.
Check whether the gap is explained by incidence or risk factors (mortality reflects incidence as well as care) before attributing it to the pathway.
Agree one concrete pathway change with a named owner and record it with the YTA quality group.
Re-measure every year; national peer reviews are held once a year (roadmap 3.2.2), and persistent gaps go to the response mechanism in roadmap 3.2.3.
actions.escalation: If the gap persists for two consecutive annual releases, report it to the regional cancer centre under roadmap action 3.2.3 (response to peer-review findings).

actions.title: Verify lung treatment, stage and MDT records
actions.owner: County oncology lead and registry/data team
actions.baseline: Lung: no treatment record: 28.9% (172 of 595), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 27.3%; also MDT recorded 0.2% vs 7.1%
actions.target: No lung treatment record back in line with the rest of Finland rate (27.3%; now 28.9%) after record reconciliation; stage recorded for at least 90% of new cases (roadmap 3.2.1)
actions.annual_volume: ≈34 patient charts to audit a year (172 patients without a treatment record over 5 years, 2019–2023)
actions.timeline: Chart audit of the latest diagnosis year within 3 months; coding fixes within 6 months; notification automation by 2030
first_90_days: Pull the list of lung cancer patients without a treatment record for the latest diagnosis year
Reconcile against oncology, surgery, radiotherapy and palliative care records
Check WZC15/WZC20 coding of MDT meetings
Report corrected records to the Finnish Cancer Registry
concrete_steps: Pull the county's lung cancer patients without any HILMO treatment record within 12 months of diagnosis and review each chart: treated in another county, treated but not coded, best supportive care decision, or died before treatment.
Check that MDT meetings are coded in HILMO with WZC15/WZC20 even when the patient is not present; the lung quality report notes that only direct patient contacts reach HILMO.

Audit the clinical cancer notification (kliininen syöpäilmoitus) to the Finnish Cancer Registry for the stage (TNM) field; nationally stage is missing for 47.7% (7,097 of 14,873, 2019–2023) of lung cancers.
Automate the clinical notification from the oncology record (roadmap 3.2.1 targets 90% automated notifications by 2030 and 90% data coverage including stage).
For breast screening referrals with a missing outcome, send the final diagnosis back to the screening register.
Send corrected records to the registry and re-run this snapshot before judging treatment rates.
actions.escalation: If the share without a record stays above the rest-of-Finland rate after reconciliation, treat it as a care gap: start a clinical review of untreated patients (pathway_coordination playbook).

actions.title: Close the loop after a colposcopy referral
actions.owner: County cervical screening and gynaecology leads
actions.baseline: Colposcopy after referral (referral proxy): 2.1% (4 of 190), 2024; rest of Finland 91.7%
actions.target: Colposcopy recorded for at least 91.7% of referred women (rest of Finland rate; now 2.1%); every high-grade referral seen within one month
actions.annual_volume: ≈186 referred women without a recorded colposcopy in 2024 (190 − 4)
actions.timeline: Reconciliation within 3 months; unit reporting agreed within 6 months; re-measure on the next annual statistics
first_90_days: Pull the list of referred women without a recorded colposcopy
Reconcile against gynaecology records and re-book non-attenders
Agree the §12.5 reporting fields with every colposcopy unit
concrete_steps: List women referred to colposcopy from programme screening without a recorded colposcopy and reconcile against gynaecology outpatient records.
Check each case against the urgency schedule in the cervical manual (Käypä hoito): HSIL or ASC-H within one month, AGC-NOS within two months, LSIL at the latest within six months.
Require colposcopy units to report to the screening organiser whether and when colposcopy was done and the colposcopic diagnosis (cervical manual §12.5).
Re-book non-attenders with a named contact person and a pre-booked appointment.
Report quarterly the share of referred women examined within the urgency window.
actions.escalation: If high-grade referrals are not seen within one month after reconciliation, escalate capacity to the collaboration-area gynaecology lead.

FICAN cervical screening quality manual 2026, §12.5 colposcopy quality monitoring

actions.title: Verify lung treatment, stage and MDT records
actions.owner: County oncology lead and registry/data team
actions.baseline: Lung: no treatment record: 43.1% (619 of 1,437), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 25.7%; also MDT recorded 1.6% vs 7.4%; also Curative lung treatment 24.3% vs 27.3%; also Breast referral outcome missing 8.4% vs 4.6%
actions.target: No lung treatment record back in line with the rest of Finland rate (25.7%; now 43.1%) after record reconciliation; stage recorded for at least 90% of new cases (roadmap 3.2.1)
actions.annual_volume: ≈124 patient charts to audit a year (619 patients without a treatment record over 5 years, 2019–2023)
actions.timeline: Chart audit of the latest diagnosis year within 3 months; coding fixes within 6 months; notification automation by 2030
first_90_days: Pull the list of lung cancer patients without a treatment record for the latest diagnosis year
Reconcile against oncology, surgery, radiotherapy and palliative care records
Check WZC15/WZC20 coding of MDT meetings
Report corrected records to the Finnish Cancer Registry
concrete_steps: Pull the county's lung cancer patients without any HILMO treatment record within 12 months of diagnosis and review each chart: treated in another county, treated but not coded, best supportive care decision, or died before treatment.
Check that MDT meetings are coded in HILMO with WZC15/WZC20 even when the patient is not present; the lung quality report notes that only direct patient contacts reach HILMO.

Audit the clinical cancer notification (kliininen syöpäilmoitus) to the Finnish Cancer Registry for the stage (TNM) field; nationally stage is missing for 47.7% (7,097 of 14,873, 2019–2023) of lung cancers.
Automate the clinical notification from the oncology record (roadmap 3.2.1 targets 90% automated notifications by 2030 and 90% data coverage including stage).
For breast screening referrals with a missing outcome, send the final diagnosis back to the screening register.
Send corrected records to the registry and re-run this snapshot before judging treatment rates.
actions.escalation: If the share without a record stays above the rest-of-Finland rate after reconciliation, treat it as a care gap: start a clinical review of untreated patients (pathway_coordination playbook).

actions.title: Peer review of a survival or mortality gap
actions.owner: County cancer centre lead with the collaboration-area (YTA) quality group
actions.baseline: Mortality: Prostate: 47.3 /100k (95% CI 42.1 /100k–53.0 /100k), 2020–2024; national 36.4 /100k; also Colorectal mortality 25.8 /100k vs 22.0 /100k
actions.target: Prostate mortality moving toward the national value (36.4 /100k; now 47.3 /100k) in the next annual Cancer in Finland release; one agreed pathway change implemented within 12 months
actions.annual_volume: ≈59 cancer deaths a year in scope (297 over 5 years, 2020–2024)
actions.timeline: Peer review within 6 months; annual re-measurement
first_90_days: Choose the peer county and agree a data-exchange template
Pull stage, diagnostic route and treatment mix for the cancer with the gap
Schedule the joint review with both counties' clinical leads
concrete_steps: Pick a peer county with a similar population profile and a better outcome for the same cancer (the snapshot lists demographic peers) and exchange aggregate pathway data. Suggested peer: Päijät-Häme (Prostate mortality 30.4 /100k).
Compare stage at diagnosis, the share with histological confirmation, the diagnostic route and the treatment mix for the cancer with the gap.
Check whether the gap is explained by incidence or risk factors (mortality reflects incidence as well as care) before attributing it to the pathway.
Agree one concrete pathway change with a named owner and record it with the YTA quality group.
Re-measure every year; national peer reviews are held once a year (roadmap 3.2.2), and persistent gaps go to the response mechanism in roadmap 3.2.3.
actions.escalation: If the gap persists for two consecutive annual releases, report it to the regional cancer centre under roadmap action 3.2.3 (response to peer-review findings).

National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 3.2.3 (responding to peer-review findings)

actions.title: Verify lung treatment, stage and MDT records
actions.owner: County oncology lead and registry/data team
actions.baseline: Lung: no treatment record: 29.8% (203 of 682), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 27.3%; also MDT recorded 0.6% vs 7.1%; also Breast referral outcome missing 26.5% vs 3.4%
actions.target: No lung treatment record back in line with the rest of Finland rate (27.3%; now 29.8%) after record reconciliation; stage recorded for at least 90% of new cases (roadmap 3.2.1)
actions.annual_volume: ≈41 patient charts to audit a year (203 patients without a treatment record over 5 years, 2019–2023)
actions.timeline: Chart audit of the latest diagnosis year within 3 months; coding fixes within 6 months; notification automation by 2030
first_90_days: Pull the list of lung cancer patients without a treatment record for the latest diagnosis year
Reconcile against oncology, surgery, radiotherapy and palliative care records
Check WZC15/WZC20 coding of MDT meetings
Report corrected records to the Finnish Cancer Registry
concrete_steps: Pull the county's lung cancer patients without any HILMO treatment record within 12 months of diagnosis and review each chart: treated in another county, treated but not coded, best supportive care decision, or died before treatment.
Check that MDT meetings are coded in HILMO with WZC15/WZC20 even when the patient is not present; the lung quality report notes that only direct patient contacts reach HILMO.

Audit the clinical cancer notification (kliininen syöpäilmoitus) to the Finnish Cancer Registry for the stage (TNM) field; nationally stage is missing for 47.7% (7,097 of 14,873, 2019–2023) of lung cancers.
Automate the clinical notification from the oncology record (roadmap 3.2.1 targets 90% automated notifications by 2030 and 90% data coverage including stage).
For breast screening referrals with a missing outcome, send the final diagnosis back to the screening register.
Send corrected records to the registry and re-run this snapshot before judging treatment rates.
actions.escalation: If the share without a record stays above the rest-of-Finland rate after reconciliation, treat it as a care gap: start a clinical review of untreated patients (pathway_coordination playbook).

actions.title: Raise screening participation with reminders and accessible invitations
actions.owner: County screening programme lead
actions.baseline: Cervical screening attendance: 71.5% (7,170 of 10,022), 2024; rest of Finland 73.6%
actions.target: Cervical screening at or above the rest of Finland rate (73.6%; now 71.5%) in the next programme round; a reminder sent to 100% of eligible non-attenders
actions.annual_volume: ≈2,852 invited people who did not attend in 2024 (10,022 − 7,170)
actions.timeline: Reminder workflow live within 3 months; effect read from the next annual screening statistics (12–18 months)
first_90_days: Name the programme owner and pull the latest non-attender list
Audit undeliverable invitations and the invitation language
Switch on the automated reminder (6 weeks breast and colorectal, 4–8 weeks cervical)
Agree monthly participation reporting with the Finnish Cancer Registry (roadmap 2.4.5)
concrete_steps: Pull the non-attender list for the latest programme round from the screening register and break it down by language (Finnish, Swedish, other), age group and postcode area.
Audit invitation delivery (undeliverable letters, outdated addresses) so delivery failures are not counted as refusals.

Automate the reminder in the invitation system: breast, a reminder invitation 6 weeks after the first (breast manual §6.4); colorectal, a reminder letter with a free replacement kit if no sample arrives within 6 weeks (colorectal manual §10.5); cervical, a reminder 4–8 weeks after the first invitation (cervical manual §8.3).
Send invitations and reminders in the person's registered language using the Finnish Cancer Registry templates (Finnish, Swedish, English), and through suomi.fi where the person has enabled it.
For cervical screening, offer a pre-booked time and place and an HPV self-sampling kit to non-attenders after the reminder (cervical manual §8.4).
Write the reminder requirements into the screening service procurement contract (roadmap action 2.4.1).
actions.escalation: If participation stays below the rest-of-Finland rate after one round with reminders, commission an equity analysis by language and area and take it to the collaboration-area (YTA) screening steering group.

actions.title: Raise screening participation with reminders and accessible invitations
actions.owner: County screening programme lead
actions.baseline: Cervical screening attendance: 70.0% (5,814 of 8,312), 2024; rest of Finland 73.6%
actions.target: Cervical screening at or above the rest of Finland rate (73.6%; now 70.0%) in the next programme round; a reminder sent to 100% of eligible non-attenders
actions.annual_volume: ≈2,498 invited people who did not attend in 2024 (8,312 − 5,814)
actions.timeline: Reminder workflow live within 3 months; effect read from the next annual screening statistics (12–18 months)
first_90_days: Name the programme owner and pull the latest non-attender list
Audit undeliverable invitations and the invitation language
Switch on the automated reminder (6 weeks breast and colorectal, 4–8 weeks cervical)
Agree monthly participation reporting with the Finnish Cancer Registry (roadmap 2.4.5)
concrete_steps: Pull the non-attender list for the latest programme round from the screening register and break it down by language (Finnish, Swedish, other), age group and postcode area.
Audit invitation delivery (undeliverable letters, outdated addresses) so delivery failures are not counted as refusals.

Automate the reminder in the invitation system: breast, a reminder invitation 6 weeks after the first (breast manual §6.4); colorectal, a reminder letter with a free replacement kit if no sample arrives within 6 weeks (colorectal manual §10.5); cervical, a reminder 4–8 weeks after the first invitation (cervical manual §8.3).
Send invitations and reminders in the person's registered language using the Finnish Cancer Registry templates (Finnish, Swedish, English), and through suomi.fi where the person has enabled it.
For cervical screening, offer a pre-booked time and place and an HPV self-sampling kit to non-attenders after the reminder (cervical manual §8.4).
Write the reminder requirements into the screening service procurement contract (roadmap action 2.4.1).
actions.escalation: If participation stays below the rest-of-Finland rate after one round with reminders, commission an equity analysis by language and area and take it to the collaboration-area (YTA) screening steering group.

citations.label: FICAN colorectal screening quality manual 2026, §10.5 reminder letter
FICAN breast screening quality manual 2026, §6.4 reminder invitation
FICAN cervical screening quality manual 2026, §8.3–8.4 reminder and self-sampling
National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 2.4.1 (quality manuals in procurement)

actions.title: Verify lung treatment, stage and MDT records
actions.owner: County oncology lead and registry/data team
actions.baseline: Lung: no treatment record: 32.0% (175 of 546), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 27.2%
actions.target: No lung treatment record back in line with the rest of Finland rate (27.2%; now 32.0%) after record reconciliation; stage recorded for at least 90% of new cases (roadmap 3.2.1)
actions.annual_volume: ≈35 patient charts to audit a year (175 patients without a treatment record over 5 years, 2019–2023)
actions.timeline: Chart audit of the latest diagnosis year within 3 months; coding fixes within 6 months; notification automation by 2030
first_90_days: Pull the list of lung cancer patients without a treatment record for the latest diagnosis year
Reconcile against oncology, surgery, radiotherapy and palliative care records
Check WZC15/WZC20 coding of MDT meetings
Report corrected records to the Finnish Cancer Registry
concrete_steps: Pull the county's lung cancer patients without any HILMO treatment record within 12 months of diagnosis and review each chart: treated in another county, treated but not coded, best supportive care decision, or died before treatment.
Check that MDT meetings are coded in HILMO with WZC15/WZC20 even when the patient is not present; the lung quality report notes that only direct patient contacts reach HILMO.

Audit the clinical cancer notification (kliininen syöpäilmoitus) to the Finnish Cancer Registry for the stage (TNM) field; nationally stage is missing for 47.7% (7,097 of 14,873, 2019–2023) of lung cancers.
Automate the clinical notification from the oncology record (roadmap 3.2.1 targets 90% automated notifications by 2030 and 90% data coverage including stage).
For breast screening referrals with a missing outcome, send the final diagnosis back to the screening register.
Send corrected records to the registry and re-run this snapshot before judging treatment rates.
actions.escalation: If the share without a record stays above the rest-of-Finland rate after reconciliation, treat it as a care gap: start a clinical review of untreated patients (pathway_coordination playbook).

citations.label: Finnish Cancer Registry, lung cancer quality report 2019–2023 (MDT recording and missing stage)
National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 3.2.1 (90% coverage incl. stage; automated clinical notifications)
Finnish Cancer Registry, clinical notification statistics by wellbeing services county

actions.title: Raise screening participation with reminders and accessible invitations
actions.owner: County screening programme lead
actions.baseline: Cervical screening attendance: 71.0% (19,198 of 27,033), 2024; rest of Finland 73.7%
actions.target: Cervical screening at or above the rest of Finland rate (73.7%; now 71.0%) in the next programme round; a reminder sent to 100% of eligible non-attenders
actions.annual_volume: ≈7,835 invited people who did not attend in 2024 (27,033 − 19,198)
actions.timeline: Reminder workflow live within 3 months; effect read from the next annual screening statistics (12–18 months)
first_90_days: Name the programme owner and pull the latest non-attender list
Audit undeliverable invitations and the invitation language
Switch on the automated reminder (6 weeks breast and colorectal, 4–8 weeks cervical)
Agree monthly participation reporting with the Finnish Cancer Registry (roadmap 2.4.5)
concrete_steps: Pull the non-attender list for the latest programme round from the screening register and break it down by language (Finnish, Swedish, other), age group and postcode area.
Audit invitation delivery (undeliverable letters, outdated addresses) so delivery failures are not counted as refusals.

Automate the reminder in the invitation system: breast, a reminder invitation 6 weeks after the first (breast manual §6.4); colorectal, a reminder letter with a free replacement kit if no sample arrives within 6 weeks (colorectal manual §10.5); cervical, a reminder 4–8 weeks after the first invitation (cervical manual §8.3).
Send invitations and reminders in the person's registered language using the Finnish Cancer Registry templates (Finnish, Swedish, English), and through suomi.fi where the person has enabled it.
For cervical screening, offer a pre-booked time and place and an HPV self-sampling kit to non-attenders after the reminder (cervical manual §8.4).
Write the reminder requirements into the screening service procurement contract (roadmap action 2.4.1).
actions.escalation: If participation stays below the rest-of-Finland rate after one round with reminders, commission an equity analysis by language and area and take it to the collaboration-area (YTA) screening steering group.

citations.label: FICAN colorectal screening quality manual 2026, §10.5 reminder letter
FICAN breast screening quality manual 2026, §6.4 reminder invitation
FICAN cervical screening quality manual 2026, §8.3–8.4 reminder and self-sampling
National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 2.4.1 (quality manuals in procurement)

actions.title: Close the loop after a positive FIT
actions.owner: County screening and endoscopy leads
actions.baseline: Colonoscopy after positive FIT (referral proxy): 70.2% (868 of 1,236), 2024; rest of Finland 73.0%
actions.target: Colonoscopy recorded for at least 73.0% of FIT positives (rest of Finland rate; now 70.2%); a documented reason for every remaining case
actions.annual_volume: ≈368 FIT positives without a recorded colonoscopy in 2024 (1,236 − 868)
actions.timeline: Reconciliation within 3 months; nurse call-back permanent; re-measure on the next annual statistics
first_90_days: Pull the list of FIT positives without a recorded colonoscopy
Reconcile against endoscopy and HILMO records and code a reason for each case
Start the two-week screening-nurse call-back
Agree monthly reporting of colonoscopy results to the screening register
concrete_steps: List every FIT-positive person in the latest programme year without a recorded colonoscopy and reconcile each against endoscopy-unit and HILMO records (colonoscopies outside the programme count as completed follow-up).

Record a reason for every unresolved case: declined, clinically excluded, examined elsewhere, moved county after the positive test (the screening chain breaks on a move, colorectal manual §11.3), or lost to follow-up.
Make the screening nurse phone every positive person who has not made contact within about two weeks, as colorectal manual §11.2.1 requires.
Send completed colonoscopies to the screening register monthly (roadmap 2.4.5) so the loop closes visibly.
Record the date of the positive result and of the colonoscopy for every case and report the median and 90th-percentile interval quarterly.
actions.escalation: If verified non-attendance persists after the call-back, review endoscopy capacity and travel distance with the collaboration-area endoscopy units and report to the YTA screening steering group.

National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 2.4.5 (monthly screening data)

actions.title: Raise screening participation with reminders and accessible invitations
actions.owner: County screening programme lead
actions.baseline: Cervical screening attendance: 68.2% (6,817 of 9,996), 2024; rest of Finland 73.7%
actions.target: Cervical screening at or above the rest of Finland rate (73.7%; now 68.2%) in the next programme round; a reminder sent to 100% of eligible non-attenders
actions.annual_volume: ≈3,179 invited people who did not attend in 2024 (9,996 − 6,817)
actions.timeline: Reminder workflow live within 3 months; effect read from the next annual screening statistics (12–18 months)
first_90_days: Name the programme owner and pull the latest non-attender list
Audit undeliverable invitations and the invitation language
Switch on the automated reminder (6 weeks breast and colorectal, 4–8 weeks cervical)
Agree monthly participation reporting with the Finnish Cancer Registry (roadmap 2.4.5)
concrete_steps: Pull the non-attender list for the latest programme round from the screening register and break it down by language (Finnish, Swedish, other), age group and postcode area.
Audit invitation delivery (undeliverable letters, outdated addresses) so delivery failures are not counted as refusals.

Automate the reminder in the invitation system: breast, a reminder invitation 6 weeks after the first (breast manual §6.4); colorectal, a reminder letter with a free replacement kit if no sample arrives within 6 weeks (colorectal manual §10.5); cervical, a reminder 4–8 weeks after the first invitation (cervical manual §8.3).
Send invitations and reminders in the person's registered language using the Finnish Cancer Registry templates (Finnish, Swedish, English), and through suomi.fi where the person has enabled it.
For cervical screening, offer a pre-booked time and place and an HPV self-sampling kit to non-attenders after the reminder (cervical manual §8.4).
Write the reminder requirements into the screening service procurement contract (roadmap action 2.4.1).
actions.escalation: If participation stays below the rest-of-Finland rate after one round with reminders, commission an equity analysis by language and area and take it to the collaboration-area (YTA) screening steering group.

citations.label: FICAN colorectal screening quality manual 2026, §10.5 reminder letter
FICAN breast screening quality manual 2026, §6.4 reminder invitation
FICAN cervical screening quality manual 2026, §8.3–8.4 reminder and self-sampling
National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 2.4.1 (quality manuals in procurement)

actions.title: Verify lung treatment, stage and MDT records
actions.owner: County oncology lead and registry/data team
actions.baseline: Lung: MDT discussion recorded: 0.3% (2 of 659), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 7.1%
actions.target: MDT recorded back in line with the rest of Finland rate (7.1%; now 0.3%) after record reconciliation; stage recorded for at least 90% of new cases (roadmap 3.2.1)
actions.annual_volume: ≈131 patient charts to audit a year (657 patients without an MDT code over 5 years, 2019–2023)
actions.timeline: Chart audit of the latest diagnosis year within 3 months; coding fixes within 6 months; notification automation by 2030
first_90_days: Pull the list of lung cancer patients without a treatment record for the latest diagnosis year
Reconcile against oncology, surgery, radiotherapy and palliative care records
Check WZC15/WZC20 coding of MDT meetings
Report corrected records to the Finnish Cancer Registry
concrete_steps: Pull the county's lung cancer patients without any HILMO treatment record within 12 months of diagnosis and review each chart: treated in another county, treated but not coded, best supportive care decision, or died before treatment.
Check that MDT meetings are coded in HILMO with WZC15/WZC20 even when the patient is not present; the lung quality report notes that only direct patient contacts reach HILMO.

Audit the clinical cancer notification (kliininen syöpäilmoitus) to the Finnish Cancer Registry for the stage (TNM) field; nationally stage is missing for 47.7% (7,097 of 14,873, 2019–2023) of lung cancers.
Automate the clinical notification from the oncology record (roadmap 3.2.1 targets 90% automated notifications by 2030 and 90% data coverage including stage).
For breast screening referrals with a missing outcome, send the final diagnosis back to the screening register.
Send corrected records to the registry and re-run this snapshot before judging treatment rates.
actions.escalation: If the share without a record stays above the rest-of-Finland rate after reconciliation, treat it as a care gap: start a clinical review of untreated patients (pathway_coordination playbook).

citations.label: Finnish Cancer Registry, lung cancer quality report 2019–2023 (MDT recording and missing stage)
National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 3.2.1 (90% coverage incl. stage; automated clinical notifications)
Finnish Cancer Registry, clinical notification statistics by wellbeing services county

actions.title: Raise screening participation with reminders and accessible invitations
actions.owner: County screening programme lead
actions.baseline: Colorectal screening attendance: 70.0% (10,098 of 14,431), 2024; rest of Finland 73.7%
actions.target: Bowel screening at or above the rest of Finland rate (73.7%; now 70.0%) in the next programme round; a reminder sent to 100% of eligible non-attenders
actions.annual_volume: ≈4,333 invited people who did not attend in 2024 (14,431 − 10,098)
actions.timeline: Reminder workflow live within 3 months; effect read from the next annual screening statistics (12–18 months)
first_90_days: Name the programme owner and pull the latest non-attender list
Audit undeliverable invitations and the invitation language
Switch on the automated reminder (6 weeks breast and colorectal, 4–8 weeks cervical)
Agree monthly participation reporting with the Finnish Cancer Registry (roadmap 2.4.5)
concrete_steps: Pull the non-attender list for the latest programme round from the screening register and break it down by language (Finnish, Swedish, other), age group and postcode area.
Audit invitation delivery (undeliverable letters, outdated addresses) so delivery failures are not counted as refusals.

Automate the reminder in the invitation system: breast, a reminder invitation 6 weeks after the first (breast manual §6.4); colorectal, a reminder letter with a free replacement kit if no sample arrives within 6 weeks (colorectal manual §10.5); cervical, a reminder 4–8 weeks after the first invitation (cervical manual §8.3).
Send invitations and reminders in the person's registered language using the Finnish Cancer Registry templates (Finnish, Swedish, English), and through suomi.fi where the person has enabled it.
For cervical screening, offer a pre-booked time and place and an HPV self-sampling kit to non-attenders after the reminder (cervical manual §8.4).
Write the reminder requirements into the screening service procurement contract (roadmap action 2.4.1).
actions.escalation: If participation stays below the rest-of-Finland rate after one round with reminders, commission an equity analysis by language and area and take it to the collaboration-area (YTA) screening steering group.

actions.title: Coordinate a fast-track lung cancer pathway
actions.owner: Primary and specialist care pathway leads (pulmonology, thoracic surgery, oncology)
actions.baseline: Lung: curative treatment: 19.3% (114 of 591), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 27.3%; also Curative : symptomatic 0.38 vs 0.70
actions.target: Curative-treatment share at or above the rest of Finland rate (27.3%; now 19.3%); about 10 more patients a year reaching curative treatment
actions.annual_volume: ≈10 patients a year short of the rest-of-Finland curative rate (118 lung cancer patients a year × 8.1 pp gap)
actions.timeline: Coordinator and referral criteria within 6 months; timestamps from month 3; curative share re-measured on the next registry quality report
first_90_days: Appoint the pathway coordinator and agree the referral criteria with primary care
Open a direct GP-to-chest-CT route for patients who meet the criteria
Start recording the four pathway timestamps for every new suspected case
Review symptomatic-care-only patients from the latest diagnosis year
concrete_steps: Agree standardised referral criteria for suspected lung cancer with primary care and a direct GP route to chest CT without a separate specialist visit first (roadmap 2.5.2: standardised referral criteria and direct investigation routes); the clinical red-flag criteria are set by the county pulmonology lead.
Name a lung cancer pathway coordinator who tracks every suspected case from referral to treatment decision and books CT, bronchoscopy or biopsy, and MDT slots.
Discuss every new lung cancer at a weekly MDT before any non-curative decision, and code the meeting (WZC15) so it is visible in HILMO.

Collect four timestamps for each patient (referral received, first specialist contact, diagnosis, treatment start) and report the median and 90th-percentile intervals monthly; Swedish SVF milestones are an external model, not a Finnish target.
Review the county's patients who received symptomatic care only within 12 months for missed curative opportunities (stage, performance status, time to diagnosis).
actions.escalation: If the curative share does not move within 12 months, take the case review to the regional cancer centre and the collaboration-area (YTA) thoracic oncology group (roadmap 3.2.3).

actions.title: Peer review of a survival or mortality gap
actions.owner: County cancer centre lead with the collaboration-area (YTA) quality group
actions.target: Colorectal mortality moving toward the national value (22.0 /100k; now 25.8 /100k) in the next annual Cancer in Finland release; one agreed pathway change implemented within 12 months
actions.annual_volume: ≈60 cancer deaths a year in scope (300 over 5 years, 2020–2024)
actions.timeline: Peer review within 6 months; annual re-measurement
first_90_days: Choose the peer county and agree a data-exchange template
Pull stage, diagnostic route and treatment mix for the cancer with the gap
Schedule the joint review with both counties' clinical leads
concrete_steps: Pick a peer county with a similar population profile and a better outcome for the same cancer (the snapshot lists demographic peers) and exchange aggregate pathway data. Suggested peer: Kanta-Häme (Colorectal mortality 21.1 /100k).
Compare stage at diagnosis, the share with histological confirmation, the diagnostic route and the treatment mix for the cancer with the gap.
Check whether the gap is explained by incidence or risk factors (mortality reflects incidence as well as care) before attributing it to the pathway.
Agree one concrete pathway change with a named owner and record it with the YTA quality group.
Re-measure every year; national peer reviews are held once a year (roadmap 3.2.2), and persistent gaps go to the response mechanism in roadmap 3.2.3.
actions.escalation: If the gap persists for two consecutive annual releases, report it to the regional cancer centre under roadmap action 3.2.3 (response to peer-review findings).

actions.title: Verify lung treatment, stage and MDT records
actions.owner: County oncology lead and registry/data team
actions.baseline: Lung: no treatment record: 42.8% (152 of 355), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 27.0%; also Curative lung treatment 18.9% vs 27.2%
actions.target: No lung treatment record back in line with the rest of Finland rate (27.0%; now 42.8%) after record reconciliation; stage recorded for at least 90% of new cases (roadmap 3.2.1)
actions.annual_volume: ≈30 patient charts to audit a year (152 patients without a treatment record over 5 years, 2019–2023)
actions.timeline: Chart audit of the latest diagnosis year within 3 months; coding fixes within 6 months; notification automation by 2030
first_90_days: Pull the list of lung cancer patients without a treatment record for the latest diagnosis year
Reconcile against oncology, surgery, radiotherapy and palliative care records
Check WZC15/WZC20 coding of MDT meetings
Report corrected records to the Finnish Cancer Registry
concrete_steps: Pull the county's lung cancer patients without any HILMO treatment record within 12 months of diagnosis and review each chart: treated in another county, treated but not coded, best supportive care decision, or died before treatment.
Check that MDT meetings are coded in HILMO with WZC15/WZC20 even when the patient is not present; the lung quality report notes that only direct patient contacts reach HILMO.

Audit the clinical cancer notification (kliininen syöpäilmoitus) to the Finnish Cancer Registry for the stage (TNM) field; nationally stage is missing for 47.7% (7,097 of 14,873, 2019–2023) of lung cancers.
Automate the clinical notification from the oncology record (roadmap 3.2.1 targets 90% automated notifications by 2030 and 90% data coverage including stage).
For breast screening referrals with a missing outcome, send the final diagnosis back to the screening register.
Send corrected records to the registry and re-run this snapshot before judging treatment rates.
actions.escalation: If the share without a record stays above the rest-of-Finland rate after reconciliation, treat it as a care gap: start a clinical review of untreated patients (pathway_coordination playbook).

citations.label: Finnish Cancer Registry, lung cancer quality report 2019–2023 (MDT recording and missing stage)
National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 3.2.1 (90% coverage incl. stage; automated clinical notifications)
Finnish Cancer Registry, clinical notification statistics by wellbeing services county

actions.title: Coordinate a fast-track lung cancer pathway
actions.owner: Primary and specialist care pathway leads (pulmonology, thoracic surgery, oncology)
actions.baseline: Lung: curative treatment: 23.4% (105 of 448), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 27.1%; also Curative : symptomatic 0.51 vs 0.69
actions.target: Curative-treatment share at or above the rest of Finland rate (27.1%; now 23.4%); about 3 more patients a year reaching curative treatment
actions.annual_volume: ≈3 patients a year short of the rest-of-Finland curative rate (90 lung cancer patients a year × 3.7 pp gap)
actions.timeline: Coordinator and referral criteria within 6 months; timestamps from month 3; curative share re-measured on the next registry quality report
first_90_days: Appoint the pathway coordinator and agree the referral criteria with primary care
Open a direct GP-to-chest-CT route for patients who meet the criteria
Start recording the four pathway timestamps for every new suspected case
Review symptomatic-care-only patients from the latest diagnosis year
concrete_steps: Agree standardised referral criteria for suspected lung cancer with primary care and a direct GP route to chest CT without a separate specialist visit first (roadmap 2.5.2: standardised referral criteria and direct investigation routes); the clinical red-flag criteria are set by the county pulmonology lead.
Name a lung cancer pathway coordinator who tracks every suspected case from referral to treatment decision and books CT, bronchoscopy or biopsy, and MDT slots.
Discuss every new lung cancer at a weekly MDT before any non-curative decision, and code the meeting (WZC15) so it is visible in HILMO.

Collect four timestamps for each patient (referral received, first specialist contact, diagnosis, treatment start) and report the median and 90th-percentile intervals monthly; Swedish SVF milestones are an external model, not a Finnish target.
Review the county's patients who received symptomatic care only within 12 months for missed curative opportunities (stage, performance status, time to diagnosis).
actions.escalation: If the curative share does not move within 12 months, take the case review to the regional cancer centre and the collaboration-area (YTA) thoracic oncology group (roadmap 3.2.3).

citations.label: National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 2.5.2 (standardised referral criteria, direct investigation routes)
National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 3.1.2 (cancer-specific pathways and target times)
Finnish Cancer Registry, lung cancer quality report 2019–2023 (only about a quarter reach curative treatment)
Hanna et al. 2020, BMJ: mortality due to cancer treatment delay (systematic review and meta-analysis)
Regional cancer centres in Sweden, standardised care pathway (SVF) example

actions.reason: Low curative share while treatment records are at least as complete as elsewhere (23.2% without a record vs 27.5%): likely treatment-access or late-detection gap.
actions.evidence_status: Policy/guidance-supported proposal; local benefit unestimated; requires clinical validation
actions.goal: Goal 3.1.2; Swedish guidance is an external model, not a Finnish target

actions.title: Verify lung treatment, stage and MDT records
actions.owner: County oncology lead and registry/data team
actions.baseline: Lung: MDT discussion recorded: 0.2% (1 of 448), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 7.0%
actions.target: MDT recorded back in line with the rest of Finland rate (7.0%; now 0.2%) after record reconciliation; stage recorded for at least 90% of new cases (roadmap 3.2.1)
actions.annual_volume: ≈89 patient charts to audit a year (447 patients without an MDT code over 5 years, 2019–2023)
actions.timeline: Chart audit of the latest diagnosis year within 3 months; coding fixes within 6 months; notification automation by 2030
first_90_days: Pull the list of lung cancer patients without a treatment record for the latest diagnosis year
Reconcile against oncology, surgery, radiotherapy and palliative care records
Check WZC15/WZC20 coding of MDT meetings
Report corrected records to the Finnish Cancer Registry
concrete_steps: Pull the county's lung cancer patients without any HILMO treatment record within 12 months of diagnosis and review each chart: treated in another county, treated but not coded, best supportive care decision, or died before treatment.
Check that MDT meetings are coded in HILMO with WZC15/WZC20 even when the patient is not present; the lung quality report notes that only direct patient contacts reach HILMO.

Audit the clinical cancer notification (kliininen syöpäilmoitus) to the Finnish Cancer Registry for the stage (TNM) field; nationally stage is missing for 47.7% (7,097 of 14,873, 2019–2023) of lung cancers.
Automate the clinical notification from the oncology record (roadmap 3.2.1 targets 90% automated notifications by 2030 and 90% data coverage including stage).
For breast screening referrals with a missing outcome, send the final diagnosis back to the screening register.
Send corrected records to the registry and re-run this snapshot before judging treatment rates.
actions.escalation: If the share without a record stays above the rest-of-Finland rate after reconciliation, treat it as a care gap: start a clinical review of untreated patients (pathway_coordination playbook).

citations.label: Finnish Cancer Registry, lung cancer quality report 2019–2023 (MDT recording and missing stage)
National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 3.2.1 (90% coverage incl. stage; automated clinical notifications)
Finnish Cancer Registry, clinical notification statistics by wellbeing services county

actions.title: Raise screening participation with reminders and accessible invitations
actions.owner: County screening programme lead
actions.baseline: Cervical screening attendance: 69.5% (8,367 of 12,037), 2024; rest of Finland 73.7%
actions.target: Cervical screening at or above the rest of Finland rate (73.7%; now 69.5%) in the next programme round; a reminder sent to 100% of eligible non-attenders
actions.annual_volume: ≈3,670 invited people who did not attend in 2024 (12,037 − 8,367)
actions.timeline: Reminder workflow live within 3 months; effect read from the next annual screening statistics (12–18 months)
first_90_days: Name the programme owner and pull the latest non-attender list
Audit undeliverable invitations and the invitation language
Switch on the automated reminder (6 weeks breast and colorectal, 4–8 weeks cervical)
Agree monthly participation reporting with the Finnish Cancer Registry (roadmap 2.4.5)
concrete_steps: Pull the non-attender list for the latest programme round from the screening register and break it down by language (Finnish, Swedish, other), age group and postcode area.
Audit invitation delivery (undeliverable letters, outdated addresses) so delivery failures are not counted as refusals.

Automate the reminder in the invitation system: breast, a reminder invitation 6 weeks after the first (breast manual §6.4); colorectal, a reminder letter with a free replacement kit if no sample arrives within 6 weeks (colorectal manual §10.5); cervical, a reminder 4–8 weeks after the first invitation (cervical manual §8.3).
Send invitations and reminders in the person's registered language using the Finnish Cancer Registry templates (Finnish, Swedish, English), and through suomi.fi where the person has enabled it.
For cervical screening, offer a pre-booked time and place and an HPV self-sampling kit to non-attenders after the reminder (cervical manual §8.4).
Write the reminder requirements into the screening service procurement contract (roadmap action 2.4.1).
actions.escalation: If participation stays below the rest-of-Finland rate after one round with reminders, commission an equity analysis by language and area and take it to the collaboration-area (YTA) screening steering group.

actions.title: Coordinate a fast-track lung cancer pathway
actions.owner: Primary and specialist care pathway leads (pulmonology, thoracic surgery, oncology)
actions.baseline: Lung: curative treatment: 24.5% (157 of 641), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 27.1%; also Curative : symptomatic 0.48 vs 0.70
actions.target: Curative-treatment share at or above the rest of Finland rate (27.1%; now 24.5%); about 3 more patients a year reaching curative treatment
actions.annual_volume: ≈3 patients a year short of the rest-of-Finland curative rate (128 lung cancer patients a year × 2.6 pp gap)
actions.timeline: Coordinator and referral criteria within 6 months; timestamps from month 3; curative share re-measured on the next registry quality report
first_90_days: Appoint the pathway coordinator and agree the referral criteria with primary care
Open a direct GP-to-chest-CT route for patients who meet the criteria
Start recording the four pathway timestamps for every new suspected case
Review symptomatic-care-only patients from the latest diagnosis year
concrete_steps: Agree standardised referral criteria for suspected lung cancer with primary care and a direct GP route to chest CT without a separate specialist visit first (roadmap 2.5.2: standardised referral criteria and direct investigation routes); the clinical red-flag criteria are set by the county pulmonology lead.
Name a lung cancer pathway coordinator who tracks every suspected case from referral to treatment decision and books CT, bronchoscopy or biopsy, and MDT slots.
Discuss every new lung cancer at a weekly MDT before any non-curative decision, and code the meeting (WZC15) so it is visible in HILMO.

Collect four timestamps for each patient (referral received, first specialist contact, diagnosis, treatment start) and report the median and 90th-percentile intervals monthly; Swedish SVF milestones are an external model, not a Finnish target.
Review the county's patients who received symptomatic care only within 12 months for missed curative opportunities (stage, performance status, time to diagnosis).
actions.escalation: If the curative share does not move within 12 months, take the case review to the regional cancer centre and the collaboration-area (YTA) thoracic oncology group (roadmap 3.2.3).

actions.title: Close the loop after a positive FIT
actions.owner: County screening and endoscopy leads
actions.baseline: Colonoscopy after positive FIT (referral proxy): 69.4% (513 of 739), 2024; rest of Finland 72.9%
actions.target: Colonoscopy recorded for at least 72.9% of FIT positives (rest of Finland rate; now 69.4%); a documented reason for every remaining case
actions.annual_volume: ≈226 FIT positives without a recorded colonoscopy in 2024 (739 − 513)
actions.timeline: Reconciliation within 3 months; nurse call-back permanent; re-measure on the next annual statistics
first_90_days: Pull the list of FIT positives without a recorded colonoscopy
Reconcile against endoscopy and HILMO records and code a reason for each case
Start the two-week screening-nurse call-back
Agree monthly reporting of colonoscopy results to the screening register
concrete_steps: List every FIT-positive person in the latest programme year without a recorded colonoscopy and reconcile each against endoscopy-unit and HILMO records (colonoscopies outside the programme count as completed follow-up).

Record a reason for every unresolved case: declined, clinically excluded, examined elsewhere, moved county after the positive test (the screening chain breaks on a move, colorectal manual §11.3), or lost to follow-up.
Make the screening nurse phone every positive person who has not made contact within about two weeks, as colorectal manual §11.2.1 requires.
Send completed colonoscopies to the screening register monthly (roadmap 2.4.5) so the loop closes visibly.
Record the date of the positive result and of the colonoscopy for every case and report the median and 90th-percentile interval quarterly.
actions.escalation: If verified non-attendance persists after the call-back, review endoscopy capacity and travel distance with the collaboration-area endoscopy units and report to the YTA screening steering group.

actions.title: Verify lung treatment, stage and MDT records
actions.owner: County oncology lead and registry/data team
actions.baseline: Lung: MDT discussion recorded: 0.2% (1 of 641), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 7.1%
actions.target: MDT recorded back in line with the rest of Finland rate (7.1%; now 0.2%) after record reconciliation; stage recorded for at least 90% of new cases (roadmap 3.2.1)
actions.annual_volume: ≈128 patient charts to audit a year (640 patients without an MDT code over 5 years, 2019–2023)
actions.timeline: Chart audit of the latest diagnosis year within 3 months; coding fixes within 6 months; notification automation by 2030
first_90_days: Pull the list of lung cancer patients without a treatment record for the latest diagnosis year
Reconcile against oncology, surgery, radiotherapy and palliative care records
Check WZC15/WZC20 coding of MDT meetings
Report corrected records to the Finnish Cancer Registry
concrete_steps: Pull the county's lung cancer patients without any HILMO treatment record within 12 months of diagnosis and review each chart: treated in another county, treated but not coded, best supportive care decision, or died before treatment.
Check that MDT meetings are coded in HILMO with WZC15/WZC20 even when the patient is not present; the lung quality report notes that only direct patient contacts reach HILMO.

Audit the clinical cancer notification (kliininen syöpäilmoitus) to the Finnish Cancer Registry for the stage (TNM) field; nationally stage is missing for 47.7% (7,097 of 14,873, 2019–2023) of lung cancers.
Automate the clinical notification from the oncology record (roadmap 3.2.1 targets 90% automated notifications by 2030 and 90% data coverage including stage).
For breast screening referrals with a missing outcome, send the final diagnosis back to the screening register.
Send corrected records to the registry and re-run this snapshot before judging treatment rates.
actions.escalation: If the share without a record stays above the rest-of-Finland rate after reconciliation, treat it as a care gap: start a clinical review of untreated patients (pathway_coordination playbook).

actions.title: Raise screening participation with reminders and accessible invitations
actions.owner: County screening programme lead
actions.baseline: Cervical screening attendance: 67.8% (5,135 of 7,572), 2024; rest of Finland 73.6%
actions.target: Cervical screening at or above the rest of Finland rate (73.6%; now 67.8%) in the next programme round; a reminder sent to 100% of eligible non-attenders
actions.annual_volume: ≈2,437 invited people who did not attend in 2024 (7,572 − 5,135)
actions.timeline: Reminder workflow live within 3 months; effect read from the next annual screening statistics (12–18 months)
first_90_days: Name the programme owner and pull the latest non-attender list
Audit undeliverable invitations and the invitation language
Switch on the automated reminder (6 weeks breast and colorectal, 4–8 weeks cervical)
Agree monthly participation reporting with the Finnish Cancer Registry (roadmap 2.4.5)
concrete_steps: Pull the non-attender list for the latest programme round from the screening register and break it down by language (Finnish, Swedish, other), age group and postcode area.
Audit invitation delivery (undeliverable letters, outdated addresses) so delivery failures are not counted as refusals.

Automate the reminder in the invitation system: breast, a reminder invitation 6 weeks after the first (breast manual §6.4); colorectal, a reminder letter with a free replacement kit if no sample arrives within 6 weeks (colorectal manual §10.5); cervical, a reminder 4–8 weeks after the first invitation (cervical manual §8.3).
Send invitations and reminders in the person's registered language using the Finnish Cancer Registry templates (Finnish, Swedish, English), and through suomi.fi where the person has enabled it.
For cervical screening, offer a pre-booked time and place and an HPV self-sampling kit to non-attenders after the reminder (cervical manual §8.4).
Write the reminder requirements into the screening service procurement contract (roadmap action 2.4.1).
actions.escalation: If participation stays below the rest-of-Finland rate after one round with reminders, commission an equity analysis by language and area and take it to the collaboration-area (YTA) screening steering group.

actions.title: Coordinate a fast-track lung cancer pathway
actions.owner: Primary and specialist care pathway leads (pulmonology, thoracic surgery, oncology)
actions.baseline: Lung: curative treatment: 21.4% (109 of 510), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 27.2%; also Curative : symptomatic 0.41 vs 0.70
actions.target: Curative-treatment share at or above the rest of Finland rate (27.2%; now 21.4%); about 6 more patients a year reaching curative treatment
actions.annual_volume: ≈6 patients a year short of the rest-of-Finland curative rate (102 lung cancer patients a year × 5.9 pp gap)
actions.timeline: Coordinator and referral criteria within 6 months; timestamps from month 3; curative share re-measured on the next registry quality report
first_90_days: Appoint the pathway coordinator and agree the referral criteria with primary care
Open a direct GP-to-chest-CT route for patients who meet the criteria
Start recording the four pathway timestamps for every new suspected case
Review symptomatic-care-only patients from the latest diagnosis year
concrete_steps: Agree standardised referral criteria for suspected lung cancer with primary care and a direct GP route to chest CT without a separate specialist visit first (roadmap 2.5.2: standardised referral criteria and direct investigation routes); the clinical red-flag criteria are set by the county pulmonology lead.
Name a lung cancer pathway coordinator who tracks every suspected case from referral to treatment decision and books CT, bronchoscopy or biopsy, and MDT slots.
Discuss every new lung cancer at a weekly MDT before any non-curative decision, and code the meeting (WZC15) so it is visible in HILMO.

Collect four timestamps for each patient (referral received, first specialist contact, diagnosis, treatment start) and report the median and 90th-percentile intervals monthly; Swedish SVF milestones are an external model, not a Finnish target.
Review the county's patients who received symptomatic care only within 12 months for missed curative opportunities (stage, performance status, time to diagnosis).
actions.escalation: If the curative share does not move within 12 months, take the case review to the regional cancer centre and the collaboration-area (YTA) thoracic oncology group (roadmap 3.2.3).

actions.title: Peer review of a survival or mortality gap
actions.owner: County cancer centre lead with the collaboration-area (YTA) quality group
actions.target: Prostate mortality moving toward the national value (36.4 /100k; now 43.3 /100k) in the next annual Cancer in Finland release; one agreed pathway change implemented within 12 months
actions.annual_volume: ≈42 cancer deaths a year in scope (209 over 5 years, 2020–2024)
actions.timeline: Peer review within 6 months; annual re-measurement
first_90_days: Choose the peer county and agree a data-exchange template
Pull stage, diagnostic route and treatment mix for the cancer with the gap
Schedule the joint review with both counties' clinical leads
concrete_steps: Pick a peer county with a similar population profile and a better outcome for the same cancer (the snapshot lists demographic peers) and exchange aggregate pathway data. Suggested peer: North Savo (Prostate mortality 32.1 /100k).
Compare stage at diagnosis, the share with histological confirmation, the diagnostic route and the treatment mix for the cancer with the gap.
Check whether the gap is explained by incidence or risk factors (mortality reflects incidence as well as care) before attributing it to the pathway.
Agree one concrete pathway change with a named owner and record it with the YTA quality group.
Re-measure every year; national peer reviews are held once a year (roadmap 3.2.2), and persistent gaps go to the response mechanism in roadmap 3.2.3.
actions.escalation: If the gap persists for two consecutive annual releases, report it to the regional cancer centre under roadmap action 3.2.3 (response to peer-review findings).
