actions.title: Raise screening participation with reminders and accessible invitations
actions.owner: County screening programme lead
actions.baseline: Cervical screening attendance: 70.2% (9,182 of 13,086), 2024; rest of Finland 73.6%
actions.target: Cervical screening at or above the rest of Finland rate (73.6%; now 70.2%) in the next programme round; a reminder sent to 100% of eligible non-attenders
actions.annual_volume: ≈3,904 invited people who did not attend in 2024 (13,086 − 9,182)
actions.timeline: Reminder workflow live within 3 months; effect read from the next annual screening statistics (12–18 months)
first_90_days: Name the programme owner and pull the latest non-attender list
Audit undeliverable invitations and the invitation language
Switch on the automated reminder (6 weeks breast and colorectal, 4–8 weeks cervical)
Agree monthly participation reporting with the Finnish Cancer Registry (roadmap 2.4.5)
concrete_steps: Pull the non-attender list for the latest programme round from the screening register and break it down by language (Finnish, Swedish, other), age group and postcode area.
Audit invitation delivery (undeliverable letters, outdated addresses) so delivery failures are not counted as refusals.

Automate the reminder in the invitation system: breast, a reminder invitation 6 weeks after the first (breast manual §6.4); colorectal, a reminder letter with a free replacement kit if no sample arrives within 6 weeks (colorectal manual §10.5); cervical, a reminder 4–8 weeks after the first invitation (cervical manual §8.3).
Send invitations and reminders in the person's registered language using the Finnish Cancer Registry templates (Finnish, Swedish, English), and through suomi.fi where the person has enabled it.
For cervical screening, offer a pre-booked time and place and an HPV self-sampling kit to non-attenders after the reminder (cervical manual §8.4).
Write the reminder requirements into the screening service procurement contract (roadmap action 2.4.1).
actions.escalation: If participation stays below the rest-of-Finland rate after one round with reminders, commission an equity analysis by language and area and take it to the collaboration-area (YTA) screening steering group.

citations.label: FICAN colorectal screening quality manual 2026, §10.5 reminder letter
FICAN breast screening quality manual 2026, §6.4 reminder invitation
FICAN cervical screening quality manual 2026, §8.3–8.4 reminder and self-sampling
National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 2.4.1 (quality manuals in procurement)

actions.title: Verify lung treatment, stage and MDT records
actions.owner: County oncology lead and registry/data team
actions.baseline: Lung: MDT discussion recorded: 3.8% (24 of 637), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 6.9%
actions.target: MDT recorded back in line with the rest of Finland rate (6.9%; now 3.8%) after record reconciliation; stage recorded for at least 90% of new cases (roadmap 3.2.1)
actions.annual_volume: ≈123 patient charts to audit a year (613 patients without an MDT code over 5 years, 2019–2023)
actions.timeline: Chart audit of the latest diagnosis year within 3 months; coding fixes within 6 months; notification automation by 2030
first_90_days: Pull the list of lung cancer patients without a treatment record for the latest diagnosis year
Reconcile against oncology, surgery, radiotherapy and palliative care records
Check WZC15/WZC20 coding of MDT meetings
Report corrected records to the Finnish Cancer Registry
concrete_steps: Pull the county's lung cancer patients without any HILMO treatment record within 12 months of diagnosis and review each chart: treated in another county, treated but not coded, best supportive care decision, or died before treatment.
Check that MDT meetings are coded in HILMO with WZC15/WZC20 even when the patient is not present; the lung quality report notes that only direct patient contacts reach HILMO.

Audit the clinical cancer notification (kliininen syöpäilmoitus) to the Finnish Cancer Registry for the stage (TNM) field; nationally stage is missing for 47.7% (7,097 of 14,873, 2019–2023) of lung cancers.
Automate the clinical notification from the oncology record (roadmap 3.2.1 targets 90% automated notifications by 2030 and 90% data coverage including stage).
For breast screening referrals with a missing outcome, send the final diagnosis back to the screening register.
Send corrected records to the registry and re-run this snapshot before judging treatment rates.
actions.escalation: If the share without a record stays above the rest-of-Finland rate after reconciliation, treat it as a care gap: start a clinical review of untreated patients (pathway_coordination playbook).

National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 3.2.1 (90% coverage incl. stage; automated clinical notifications)
Finnish Cancer Registry, clinical notification statistics by wellbeing services county

actions.title: Peer review of a survival or mortality gap
actions.owner: County cancer centre lead with the collaboration-area (YTA) quality group
actions.target: Colorectal mortality moving toward the national value (22.0 /100k; now 24.7 /100k) in the next annual Cancer in Finland release; one agreed pathway change implemented within 12 months
actions.annual_volume: ≈62 cancer deaths a year in scope (312 over 5 years, 2020–2024)
actions.timeline: Peer review within 6 months; annual re-measurement
first_90_days: Choose the peer county and agree a data-exchange template
Pull stage, diagnostic route and treatment mix for the cancer with the gap
Schedule the joint review with both counties' clinical leads
concrete_steps: Pick a peer county with a similar population profile and a better outcome for the same cancer (the snapshot lists demographic peers) and exchange aggregate pathway data. Suggested peer: North Karelia (Colorectal mortality 18.8 /100k).
Compare stage at diagnosis, the share with histological confirmation, the diagnostic route and the treatment mix for the cancer with the gap.
Check whether the gap is explained by incidence or risk factors (mortality reflects incidence as well as care) before attributing it to the pathway.
Agree one concrete pathway change with a named owner and record it with the YTA quality group.
Re-measure every year; national peer reviews are held once a year (roadmap 3.2.2), and persistent gaps go to the response mechanism in roadmap 3.2.3.
actions.escalation: If the gap persists for two consecutive annual releases, report it to the regional cancer centre under roadmap action 3.2.3 (response to peer-review findings).

first_90_days: Break down screening uptake by registered language (Finnish, Swedish, other) and municipality
Confirm monthly screening-register feeds (roadmap 2.4.5) and TNM stage notification coverage
Enable prospective 4-timestamp pathway logging for new lung, breast and colorectal referrals
concrete_steps: Stratify the county's latest breast, cervical and colorectal screening attendance by native language (Finnish, Swedish, other) and municipality so strong county averages do not mask pockets with 20+ pp lower uptake.

Start prospective recording of the four cancer-pathway timestamps (referral received, first specialist contact, diagnosis, treatment start) to close the national referral-delay data gap (roadmap 3.1.2).

actions.title: Raise screening participation with reminders and accessible invitations
actions.owner: County screening programme lead
actions.baseline: Cervical screening attendance: 69.1% (2,152 of 3,114), 2024; rest of Finland 73.5%
actions.target: Cervical screening at or above the rest of Finland rate (73.5%; now 69.1%) in the next programme round; a reminder sent to 100% of eligible non-attenders
actions.annual_volume: ≈962 invited people who did not attend in 2024 (3,114 − 2,152)
actions.timeline: Reminder workflow live within 3 months; effect read from the next annual screening statistics (12–18 months)
first_90_days: Name the programme owner and pull the latest non-attender list
Audit undeliverable invitations and the invitation language
Switch on the automated reminder (6 weeks breast and colorectal, 4–8 weeks cervical)
Agree monthly participation reporting with the Finnish Cancer Registry (roadmap 2.4.5)
concrete_steps: Pull the non-attender list for the latest programme round from the screening register and break it down by language (Finnish, Swedish, other), age group and postcode area.
Audit invitation delivery (undeliverable letters, outdated addresses) so delivery failures are not counted as refusals.

Automate the reminder in the invitation system: breast, a reminder invitation 6 weeks after the first (breast manual §6.4); colorectal, a reminder letter with a free replacement kit if no sample arrives within 6 weeks (colorectal manual §10.5); cervical, a reminder 4–8 weeks after the first invitation (cervical manual §8.3).
Send invitations and reminders in the person's registered language using the Finnish Cancer Registry templates (Finnish, Swedish, English), and through suomi.fi where the person has enabled it.
For cervical screening, offer a pre-booked time and place and an HPV self-sampling kit to non-attenders after the reminder (cervical manual §8.4).
Write the reminder requirements into the screening service procurement contract (roadmap action 2.4.1).
actions.escalation: If participation stays below the rest-of-Finland rate after one round with reminders, commission an equity analysis by language and area and take it to the collaboration-area (YTA) screening steering group.

actions.annual_volume: ≈29 patient charts to audit a year (146 patients without an MDT code over 5 years, 2019–2023)
actions.timeline: Chart audit of the latest diagnosis year within 3 months; coding fixes within 6 months; notification automation by 2030
first_90_days: Pull the list of lung cancer patients without a treatment record for the latest diagnosis year
Reconcile against oncology, surgery, radiotherapy and palliative care records
Check WZC15/WZC20 coding of MDT meetings
Report corrected records to the Finnish Cancer Registry
concrete_steps: Pull the county's lung cancer patients without any HILMO treatment record within 12 months of diagnosis and review each chart: treated in another county, treated but not coded, best supportive care decision, or died before treatment.
Check that MDT meetings are coded in HILMO with WZC15/WZC20 even when the patient is not present; the lung quality report notes that only direct patient contacts reach HILMO.

Audit the clinical cancer notification (kliininen syöpäilmoitus) to the Finnish Cancer Registry for the stage (TNM) field; nationally stage is missing for 47.7% (7,097 of 14,873, 2019–2023) of lung cancers.
Automate the clinical notification from the oncology record (roadmap 3.2.1 targets 90% automated notifications by 2030 and 90% data coverage including stage).
For breast screening referrals with a missing outcome, send the final diagnosis back to the screening register.
Send corrected records to the registry and re-run this snapshot before judging treatment rates.
actions.escalation: If the share without a record stays above the rest-of-Finland rate after reconciliation, treat it as a care gap: start a clinical review of untreated patients (pathway_coordination playbook).

actions.title: Coordinate a fast-track lung cancer pathway
actions.owner: Primary and specialist care pathway leads (pulmonology, thoracic surgery, oncology)
actions.baseline: Lung: curative treatment: 23.6% (248 of 1,050), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 27.3%
actions.target: Curative-treatment share at or above the rest of Finland rate (27.3%; now 23.6%); about 8 more patients a year reaching curative treatment
actions.annual_volume: ≈8 patients a year short of the rest-of-Finland curative rate (210 lung cancer patients a year × 3.7 pp gap)
actions.timeline: Coordinator and referral criteria within 6 months; timestamps from month 3; curative share re-measured on the next registry quality report
first_90_days: Appoint the pathway coordinator and agree the referral criteria with primary care
Open a direct GP-to-chest-CT route for patients who meet the criteria
Start recording the four pathway timestamps for every new suspected case
Review symptomatic-care-only patients from the latest diagnosis year
concrete_steps: Agree standardised referral criteria for suspected lung cancer with primary care and a direct GP route to chest CT without a separate specialist visit first (roadmap 2.5.2: standardised referral criteria and direct investigation routes); the clinical red-flag criteria are set by the county pulmonology lead.
Name a lung cancer pathway coordinator who tracks every suspected case from referral to treatment decision and books CT, bronchoscopy or biopsy, and MDT slots.
Discuss every new lung cancer at a weekly MDT before any non-curative decision, and code the meeting (WZC15) so it is visible in HILMO.

Collect four timestamps for each patient (referral received, first specialist contact, diagnosis, treatment start) and report the median and 90th-percentile intervals monthly; Swedish SVF milestones are an external model, not a Finnish target.
Review the county's patients who received symptomatic care only within 12 months for missed curative opportunities (stage, performance status, time to diagnosis).
actions.escalation: If the curative share does not move within 12 months, take the case review to the regional cancer centre and the collaboration-area (YTA) thoracic oncology group (roadmap 3.2.3).

actions.title: Peer review of a survival or mortality gap
actions.owner: County cancer centre lead with the collaboration-area (YTA) quality group
actions.target: Lung (women) mortality moving toward the national value (24.7 /100k; now 27.8 /100k) in the next annual Cancer in Finland release; one agreed pathway change implemented within 12 months
actions.annual_volume: ≈64 cancer deaths a year in scope (319 over 5 years, 2020–2024)
actions.timeline: Peer review within 6 months; annual re-measurement
first_90_days: Choose the peer county and agree a data-exchange template
Pull stage, diagnostic route and treatment mix for the cancer with the gap
Schedule the joint review with both counties' clinical leads
concrete_steps: Pick a peer county with a similar population profile and a better outcome for the same cancer (the snapshot lists demographic peers) and exchange aggregate pathway data. Suggested peer: North Savo (Lung (women) mortality 16.9 /100k).
Compare stage at diagnosis, the share with histological confirmation, the diagnostic route and the treatment mix for the cancer with the gap.
Check whether the gap is explained by incidence or risk factors (mortality reflects incidence as well as care) before attributing it to the pathway.
Agree one concrete pathway change with a named owner and record it with the YTA quality group.
Re-measure every year; national peer reviews are held once a year (roadmap 3.2.2), and persistent gaps go to the response mechanism in roadmap 3.2.3.
actions.escalation: If the gap persists for two consecutive annual releases, report it to the regional cancer centre under roadmap action 3.2.3 (response to peer-review findings).

actions.title: Verify lung treatment, stage and MDT records
actions.owner: County oncology lead and registry/data team
actions.baseline: Lung: MDT discussion recorded: 1.1% (12 of 1,050), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 7.3%
actions.target: MDT recorded back in line with the rest of Finland rate (7.3%; now 1.1%) after record reconciliation; stage recorded for at least 90% of new cases (roadmap 3.2.1)
actions.annual_volume: ≈208 patient charts to audit a year (1,038 patients without an MDT code over 5 years, 2019–2023)
actions.timeline: Chart audit of the latest diagnosis year within 3 months; coding fixes within 6 months; notification automation by 2030
first_90_days: Pull the list of lung cancer patients without a treatment record for the latest diagnosis year
Reconcile against oncology, surgery, radiotherapy and palliative care records
Check WZC15/WZC20 coding of MDT meetings
Report corrected records to the Finnish Cancer Registry
concrete_steps: Pull the county's lung cancer patients without any HILMO treatment record within 12 months of diagnosis and review each chart: treated in another county, treated but not coded, best supportive care decision, or died before treatment.
Check that MDT meetings are coded in HILMO with WZC15/WZC20 even when the patient is not present; the lung quality report notes that only direct patient contacts reach HILMO.

Audit the clinical cancer notification (kliininen syöpäilmoitus) to the Finnish Cancer Registry for the stage (TNM) field; nationally stage is missing for 47.7% (7,097 of 14,873, 2019–2023) of lung cancers.
Automate the clinical notification from the oncology record (roadmap 3.2.1 targets 90% automated notifications by 2030 and 90% data coverage including stage).
For breast screening referrals with a missing outcome, send the final diagnosis back to the screening register.
Send corrected records to the registry and re-run this snapshot before judging treatment rates.
actions.escalation: If the share without a record stays above the rest-of-Finland rate after reconciliation, treat it as a care gap: start a clinical review of untreated patients (pathway_coordination playbook).

actions.title: Close the loop after a colposcopy referral
actions.owner: County cervical screening and gynaecology leads
actions.baseline: Colposcopy after referral (referral proxy): 73.3% (107 of 146), 2024; rest of Finland 85.4%
actions.target: Colposcopy recorded for at least 85.4% of referred women (rest of Finland rate; now 73.3%); every high-grade referral seen within one month
actions.annual_volume: ≈39 referred women without a recorded colposcopy in 2024 (146 − 107)
actions.timeline: Reconciliation within 3 months; unit reporting agreed within 6 months; re-measure on the next annual statistics
first_90_days: Pull the list of referred women without a recorded colposcopy
Reconcile against gynaecology records and re-book non-attenders
Agree the §12.5 reporting fields with every colposcopy unit
concrete_steps: List women referred to colposcopy from programme screening without a recorded colposcopy and reconcile against gynaecology outpatient records.
Check each case against the urgency schedule in the cervical manual (Käypä hoito): HSIL or ASC-H within one month, AGC-NOS within two months, LSIL at the latest within six months.
Require colposcopy units to report to the screening organiser whether and when colposcopy was done and the colposcopic diagnosis (cervical manual §12.5).
Re-book non-attenders with a named contact person and a pre-booked appointment.
Report quarterly the share of referred women examined within the urgency window.
actions.escalation: If high-grade referrals are not seen within one month after reconciliation, escalate capacity to the collaboration-area gynaecology lead.

actions.title: Close the loop after a positive FIT
actions.owner: County screening and endoscopy leads
actions.baseline: Colonoscopy after positive FIT (referral proxy): 65.0% (182 of 280), 2024; rest of Finland 72.9%
actions.target: Colonoscopy recorded for at least 72.9% of FIT positives (rest of Finland rate; now 65.0%); a documented reason for every remaining case
actions.annual_volume: ≈98 FIT positives without a recorded colonoscopy in 2024 (280 − 182)
actions.timeline: Reconciliation within 3 months; nurse call-back permanent; re-measure on the next annual statistics
first_90_days: Pull the list of FIT positives without a recorded colonoscopy
Reconcile against endoscopy and HILMO records and code a reason for each case
Start the two-week screening-nurse call-back
Agree monthly reporting of colonoscopy results to the screening register
concrete_steps: List every FIT-positive person in the latest programme year without a recorded colonoscopy and reconcile each against endoscopy-unit and HILMO records (colonoscopies outside the programme count as completed follow-up).

Record a reason for every unresolved case: declined, clinically excluded, examined elsewhere, moved county after the positive test (the screening chain breaks on a move, colorectal manual §11.3), or lost to follow-up.
Make the screening nurse phone every positive person who has not made contact within about two weeks, as colorectal manual §11.2.1 requires.
Send completed colonoscopies to the screening register monthly (roadmap 2.4.5) so the loop closes visibly.
Record the date of the positive result and of the colonoscopy for every case and report the median and 90th-percentile interval quarterly.
actions.escalation: If verified non-attendance persists after the call-back, review endoscopy capacity and travel distance with the collaboration-area endoscopy units and report to the YTA screening steering group.

actions.title: Peer review of a survival or mortality gap
actions.owner: County cancer centre lead with the collaboration-area (YTA) quality group
actions.baseline: Mortality: Lung (men): 64.1 /100k (95% CI 57.6 /100k–71.3 /100k), 2020–2024; national 50.1 /100k; also Lung (women) mortality 32.4 /100k vs 24.7 /100k; also Prostate mortality 44.7 /100k vs 36.4 /100k
actions.target: Lung (men) mortality moving toward the national value (50.1 /100k; now 64.1 /100k) in the next annual Cancer in Finland release; one agreed pathway change implemented within 12 months
actions.annual_volume: ≈70 cancer deaths a year in scope (349 over 5 years, 2020–2024)
actions.timeline: Peer review within 6 months; annual re-measurement
first_90_days: Choose the peer county and agree a data-exchange template
Pull stage, diagnostic route and treatment mix for the cancer with the gap
Schedule the joint review with both counties' clinical leads
concrete_steps: Pick a peer county with a similar population profile and a better outcome for the same cancer (the snapshot lists demographic peers) and exchange aggregate pathway data. Suggested peer: North Savo (Lung (men) mortality 42.6 /100k).
Compare stage at diagnosis, the share with histological confirmation, the diagnostic route and the treatment mix for the cancer with the gap.
Check whether the gap is explained by incidence or risk factors (mortality reflects incidence as well as care) before attributing it to the pathway.
Agree one concrete pathway change with a named owner and record it with the YTA quality group.
Re-measure every year; national peer reviews are held once a year (roadmap 3.2.2), and persistent gaps go to the response mechanism in roadmap 3.2.3.
actions.escalation: If the gap persists for two consecutive annual releases, report it to the regional cancer centre under roadmap action 3.2.3 (response to peer-review findings).

actions.title: Verify lung treatment, stage and MDT records
actions.owner: County oncology lead and registry/data team
actions.baseline: Lung: no treatment record: 33.8% (240 of 710), 2019–2023; rest of Finland 27.1%; also Curative : symptomatic 0.41 vs 0.70; also MDT recorded 3.0% vs 7.0%; also Curative lung treatment 18.4% vs 27.5%
actions.target: No lung treatment record back in line with the rest of Finland rate (27.1%; now 33.8%) after record reconciliation; stage recorded for at least 90% of new cases (roadmap 3.2.1)
actions.annual_volume: ≈48 patient charts to audit a year (240 patients without a treatment record over 5 years, 2019–2023)
actions.timeline: Chart audit of the latest diagnosis year within 3 months; coding fixes within 6 months; notification automation by 2030
first_90_days: Pull the list of lung cancer patients without a treatment record for the latest diagnosis year
Reconcile against oncology, surgery, radiotherapy and palliative care records
Check WZC15/WZC20 coding of MDT meetings
Report corrected records to the Finnish Cancer Registry
concrete_steps: Pull the county's lung cancer patients without any HILMO treatment record within 12 months of diagnosis and review each chart: treated in another county, treated but not coded, best supportive care decision, or died before treatment.
Check that MDT meetings are coded in HILMO with WZC15/WZC20 even when the patient is not present; the lung quality report notes that only direct patient contacts reach HILMO.

Audit the clinical cancer notification (kliininen syöpäilmoitus) to the Finnish Cancer Registry for the stage (TNM) field; nationally stage is missing for 47.7% (7,097 of 14,873, 2019–2023) of lung cancers.
Automate the clinical notification from the oncology record (roadmap 3.2.1 targets 90% automated notifications by 2030 and 90% data coverage including stage).
For breast screening referrals with a missing outcome, send the final diagnosis back to the screening register.
Send corrected records to the registry and re-run this snapshot before judging treatment rates.
actions.escalation: If the share without a record stays above the rest-of-Finland rate after reconciliation, treat it as a care gap: start a clinical review of untreated patients (pathway_coordination playbook).

actions.title: Raise screening participation with reminders and accessible invitations
actions.owner: County screening programme lead
actions.baseline: Breast screening attendance: 74.3% (28,686 of 38,630), 2024; rest of Finland 82.5%; also Bowel screening 69.6% vs 74.0%; also Cervical screening 71.7% vs 73.8%
actions.target: Breast screening at or above the rest of Finland rate (82.5%; now 74.3%) in the next programme round; a reminder sent to 100% of eligible non-attenders
actions.annual_volume: ≈9,944 invited people who did not attend in 2024 (38,630 − 28,686)
actions.timeline: Reminder workflow live within 3 months; effect read from the next annual screening statistics (12–18 months)
first_90_days: Name the programme owner and pull the latest non-attender list
Audit undeliverable invitations and the invitation language
Switch on the automated reminder (6 weeks breast and colorectal, 4–8 weeks cervical)
Agree monthly participation reporting with the Finnish Cancer Registry (roadmap 2.4.5)
concrete_steps: Pull the non-attender list for the latest programme round from the screening register and break it down by language (Finnish, Swedish, other), age group and postcode area.
Audit invitation delivery (undeliverable letters, outdated addresses) so delivery failures are not counted as refusals.

Automate the reminder in the invitation system: breast, a reminder invitation 6 weeks after the first (breast manual §6.4); colorectal, a reminder letter with a free replacement kit if no sample arrives within 6 weeks (colorectal manual §10.5); cervical, a reminder 4–8 weeks after the first invitation (cervical manual §8.3).
Send invitations and reminders in the person's registered language using the Finnish Cancer Registry templates (Finnish, Swedish, English), and through suomi.fi where the person has enabled it.
For cervical screening, offer a pre-booked time and place and an HPV self-sampling kit to non-attenders after the reminder (cervical manual §8.4).
Write the reminder requirements into the screening service procurement contract (roadmap action 2.4.1).
actions.escalation: If participation stays below the rest-of-Finland rate after one round with reminders, commission an equity analysis by language and area and take it to the collaboration-area (YTA) screening steering group.

FICAN cervical screening quality manual 2026, §8.3–8.4 reminder and self-sampling
National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 2.4.1 (quality manuals in procurement)

actions.title: Close the loop after a positive FIT
actions.owner: County screening and endoscopy leads
actions.baseline: Colonoscopy after positive FIT (referral proxy): 67.8% (870 of 1,284), 2024; rest of Finland 73.2%
actions.target: Colonoscopy recorded for at least 73.2% of FIT positives (rest of Finland rate; now 67.8%); a documented reason for every remaining case
actions.annual_volume: ≈414 FIT positives without a recorded colonoscopy in 2024 (1,284 − 870)
actions.timeline: Reconciliation within 3 months; nurse call-back permanent; re-measure on the next annual statistics
first_90_days: Pull the list of FIT positives without a recorded colonoscopy
Reconcile against endoscopy and HILMO records and code a reason for each case
Start the two-week screening-nurse call-back
Agree monthly reporting of colonoscopy results to the screening register
concrete_steps: List every FIT-positive person in the latest programme year without a recorded colonoscopy and reconcile each against endoscopy-unit and HILMO records (colonoscopies outside the programme count as completed follow-up).

Record a reason for every unresolved case: declined, clinically excluded, examined elsewhere, moved county after the positive test (the screening chain breaks on a move, colorectal manual §11.3), or lost to follow-up.
Make the screening nurse phone every positive person who has not made contact within about two weeks, as colorectal manual §11.2.1 requires.
Send completed colonoscopies to the screening register monthly (roadmap 2.4.5) so the loop closes visibly.
Record the date of the positive result and of the colonoscopy for every case and report the median and 90th-percentile interval quarterly.
actions.escalation: If verified non-attendance persists after the call-back, review endoscopy capacity and travel distance with the collaboration-area endoscopy units and report to the YTA screening steering group.

method.comparator: Leave-one-out ("rest of Finland"): (national n − county n) / (national d − county d) for every indicator with published counts; age-standardised survival and mortality use the published national value. Lung comparators pool published counties; the MDT comparator covers the 18 reporting counties only.
method.signal: A county is flagged when the comparator lies outside the county 95% interval (Wilson for proportions, published CI for rates, log-scale Katz CI for the curative:symptomatic ratio). Exploratory rule; comparator uncertainty and multiple comparisons are not modelled.
method.lung_rule: Low curative lung treatment is "verify" when the county no-record share is above its comparator, otherwise "act" (likely treatment-access or late-detection gap).
method.act_rule: Other adverse signals are "act" when no quality check fails and at most one warns (two if the signal persisted across at least three annual releases); otherwise "verify". Recording indicators are always "verify".

playbooks.title: Raise screening participation with reminders and accessible invitations
playbooks.trigger: Low participation after checking invitation delivery and cohort composition
playbooks.proposal: Audit invitations, provide appropriate language materials, and implement the screening reminder workflow
concrete_steps: Pull the non-attender list for the latest programme round from the screening register and break it down by language (Finnish, Swedish, other), age group and postcode area.
Audit invitation delivery (undeliverable letters, outdated addresses) so delivery failures are not counted as refusals.

Automate the reminder in the invitation system: breast, a reminder invitation 6 weeks after the first (breast manual §6.4); colorectal, a reminder letter with a free replacement kit if no sample arrives within 6 weeks (colorectal manual §10.5); cervical, a reminder 4–8 weeks after the first invitation (cervical manual §8.3).
Send invitations and reminders in the person's registered language using the Finnish Cancer Registry templates (Finnish, Swedish, English), and through suomi.fi where the person has enabled it.
For cervical screening, offer a pre-booked time and place and an HPV self-sampling kit to non-attenders after the reminder (cervical manual §8.4).
Write the reminder requirements into the screening service procurement contract (roadmap action 2.4.1).

playbooks.title: Coordinate a fast-track lung cancer pathway
playbooks.trigger: Curative lung treatment share clearly below the rest of Finland while treatment records are at least as complete as elsewhere
playbooks.proposal: Pilot a pathway coordinator and standardised milestones from suspicion to treatment; review untreated patients with clinical teams and collect aggregate timestamp quality and interval measures
playbooks.owner: Primary and specialist care pathway leads (pulmonology, thoracic surgery, oncology)
measure: share of patients reaching curative treatment
median and p90 interval from referral to treatment
eligible patients within the cancer-specific target
concrete_steps: Agree standardised referral criteria for suspected lung cancer with primary care and a direct GP route to chest CT without a separate specialist visit first (roadmap 2.5.2: standardised referral criteria and direct investigation routes); the clinical red-flag criteria are set by the county pulmonology lead.
Name a lung cancer pathway coordinator who tracks every suspected case from referral to treatment decision and books CT, bronchoscopy or biopsy, and MDT slots.
Discuss every new lung cancer at a weekly MDT before any non-curative decision, and code the meeting (WZC15) so it is visible in HILMO.

Collect four timestamps for each patient (referral received, first specialist contact, diagnosis, treatment start) and report the median and 90th-percentile intervals monthly; Swedish SVF milestones are an external model, not a Finnish target.
Review the county's patients who received symptomatic care only within 12 months for missed curative opportunities (stage, performance status, time to diagnosis).

playbooks.timeline: Coordinator and referral criteria within 6 months; timestamps from month 3; curative share re-measured on the next registry quality report

Open a direct GP-to-chest-CT route for patients who meet the criteria
Start recording the four pathway timestamps for every new suspected case
Review symptomatic-care-only patients from the latest diagnosis year
playbooks.escalation: If the curative share does not move within 12 months, take the case review to the regional cancer centre and the collaboration-area (YTA) thoracic oncology group (roadmap 3.2.3).

playbooks.title: Peer review of a survival or mortality gap
playbooks.trigger: Survival below or mortality above the national comparator, outside the county interval
playbooks.proposal: Run a structured peer review with a comparable county that has better outcomes: compare stage at diagnosis, diagnostic route and treatment mix, agree one pathway change, and re-measure annually
playbooks.owner: County cancer centre lead with the collaboration-area (YTA) quality group
concrete_steps: Pick a peer county with a similar population profile and a better outcome for the same cancer (the snapshot lists demographic peers) and exchange aggregate pathway data.
Compare stage at diagnosis, the share with histological confirmation, the diagnostic route and the treatment mix for the cancer with the gap.
Check whether the gap is explained by incidence or risk factors (mortality reflects incidence as well as care) before attributing it to the pathway.
Agree one concrete pathway change with a named owner and record it with the YTA quality group.
Re-measure every year; national peer reviews are held once a year (roadmap 3.2.2), and persistent gaps go to the response mechanism in roadmap 3.2.3.

playbooks.timeline: Peer review within 6 months; annual re-measurement

Pull stage, diagnostic route and treatment mix for the cancer with the gap
Schedule the joint review with both counties' clinical leads
playbooks.escalation: If the gap persists for two consecutive annual releases, report it to the regional cancer centre under roadmap action 3.2.3 (response to peer-review findings).

data_gaps.what: Primary → specialist referral timestamps and waiting times
data_gaps.why: No cancer-specific referral-delay series is published by county; THL Sotkanet and the specialist waiting-time endpoint returned HTTP 403 during collection. The referral stage uses proxies only.
Stage is missing for 47.7% of lung cancers 2019–2023 nationally (lung quality report, Taulukko 4 (section 4.1.3)); county stage tables are published only as images.

limitations: Aggregate, observational data: verdicts are triage signals, not proof of cause or of care quality.
Missing treatment records do not prove absence of treatment.
Lung treatment categories overlap; no stage, age or comorbidity adjustment.
Survival and mortality are age-standardised only and compared with the national value (the county is included).
Referral-stage indicators are proxies; no referral-delay measure exists in public data.
Åland (HVA91) is outside the published lung and outcome tables and is covered by screening only in some years.
